transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, so, I guess what brings me in is... well, it's work stuff, mostly. I'm a supervisor for a sales team—not retail, like, corporate sales—and I just... I keep making these really, really dumb mistakes on my sales reports. It's driving me absolutely crazy. 

Like, I'll be looking right at the team dashboard, right? Just pulling the weekly metrics for the guys like I always do, and I'll somehow end up copying the completely wrong numbers into the final spreadsheet. Or, you know, we have these compliance procedures I'm supposed to check over for my team, just to make sure everything is squared away before we submit, and I'll just completely miss a line. Just skip right over it. 

And the most frustrating part—the part that really made me realize I need to talk to somebody—is that I'll sit there and review it. I'll literally tell myself, "Okay, let's go over this one more time so we don't look stupid," and I still miss it! Even when I thought I went over it with a fine-tooth comb, my manager will flag it later and I'm just staring at the screen wondering how on earth I didn't see it. It makes me look so incompetent, and I've been trying so hard to double-check everything, but it just keeps happening, over and over, and I just don't get why my brain is doing this.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or making careless mistakes when you were growing up, like back in school?

Oh, man. Yeah. Honestly, yes. It's funny you ask that because my mom actually still brings this up. We were just talking about it not that long ago, actually, looking at some old boxes. She kept all these old report cards and notes from my teachers from back in, like, elementary school. And it's wild to think about because the teachers were always writing notes home saying the exact same kind of things I'm dealing with now. 

They'd say I was constantly rushing through my work. Like, I'd finish a worksheet way before anyone else, but half the answers were wrong because I just blasted through it without reading the instructions properly. Or I'd actually do the work, spend all evening on it at the kitchen table, and then completely lose the homework by the next morning. Just poof, gone. It would be crumpled up at the very bottom of my backpack under a gym shirt or something, and I'd get a zero even though I did it. 

And it wasn't just the careless mistakes with the work, either. The notes were always, always about how I was talking out of turn. I just couldn't keep my mouth shut if I had a thought, I'd just blurt it out in the middle of a lesson while the teacher was still talking. And staying in my chair? Forget about it. They had to constantly remind me to sit down. I'd be up sharpening my pencil for the fifth time, or leaning way over to talk to my buddy at the next desk, or just standing up at my desk for absolutely no reason. It was just this constant loop of "sit down, stop talking, where is your assignment." 

So, yeah, I was definitely like this as a kid too. It's just that back then, the stakes were, you know, a spelling grade or missing recess, and now it's my actual career and my team's corporate metrics on the line, which is why it's stressing me out so much more now, you know? But yeah, the teachers definitely saw it all back then.
